absent: Full layout and locking of VM arch state outside the routed tail range.
Vendor specific behavior and return contracts for most operations table hooks.
Implementation and synchronization of static call dispatch.
Contents of generic VM and VCPU statistics structures.
Hyper-V TDP root lifecycle and assist page protocol.
Conditions selecting between SMM and non SMM memslot configurations.
Confidential guest hypercall ABI beyond fallback error.
Async page fault token allocation and completion protocol.

findings.text: Tail of VM scoped arch state tracks shadow root allocation, forced external write tracking metadata, optional Hyper-V TDP root with assist page, VM wide maximum vCPU identifier for sizing, a flag disabling NX huge pages, caches for eager splitting of shadow pages and headers, a descriptor cache for rmap work during splits, direct mapping bits, and CPU dirty log size where zero means unsupported or disabled.
Caches used for eager splitting of shadow pages, page headers and rmap descriptors require holding the VM slots lock while allocating during splits.
Minimum object count for the split descriptor cache equals one more than the number of entries in one page table page, covering per leaf additions plus one parent linkage extension.

VM statistics combine generic counters with MMU behavior counts for zapped shadows, pte writes, flooded and recycled pages, cache misses, unsync and live shadow pages, per size page tallies exposed both as named atomics and as an indexed array, plus NX large page splits and maxima for hash collisions and rmap size.

VCPU statistics combine generic counters with page fault outcomes, TLB activity, exit classification including IO MMIO signals windows halts and IRQ related exits, host state and FPU reloads, emulation results, hypercalls, IRQ and NMI injections, event requests, nested runs, directed yield attempts and results, preemption reports, guest mode time and notify window exits.
MSR access descriptor carries whether the access was host initiated together with register index and 64 bit value exchanged.
Local APIC interrupt request descriptor carries vector, delivery and destination modes, level and trigger state, shorthand, destination identifier and MSI redirection hint.
Run control flags occupy the low three bits, requesting immediate exit, loading of guest DR6, and loading of debug control state.

Vendor operations table provides the x86 virtualization abstraction covering CPU compatibility and enable, VM and VCPU lifecycle and sizing, guest entry preparation, control register segment descriptor debug and flag access with validation, several TLB invalidation scopes, run and exit handling with emulation helpers, interrupt shadow and injection with NMI and virtual NMI support, APIC virtualization, TSS and identity map setup, memory type queries, MMU root loading and external table hooks, TSC handling, diagnostic info, intercept decisions, dirty logging, blocking notifications, posted interrupts, timers, machine check, optional SMM, memory encryption, feature queries, SIPI delivery and guest memory conversion.

Nested operations describe second level guest support including leaving nested mode, recognizing exception exits, checking and advertising pending events, triple fault handling, state save and restore with paging helpers, dirty logging writes, nested GPA translation with fault reporting, and enlightened VMCS enable version and synthetic exit injection.
Init operations bundle one time hardware setup, Intel PT interrupt handling, and pointers to active runtime operations, performance monitoring operations and nested operations.
Asynchronous page fault context records a token, faulting frame number, faulting address space root, whether mapping was direct, and associated error code.
Vendor operation invocation goes through a static call trampoline keyed by operation name, with declaration helpers for required, optional and optional zero returning variants.
Nested operation invocation uses a parallel static call namespace with required, optional and zero default declaration helpers.
VM allocation reserves zeroed accounted kernel memory sized by the vendor specific VM size field.
Remote TLB flush helpers succeed when a vendor flush hook exists and reports success, otherwise report unsupported; the ranged variant requires its hook and forwards frame number and page count.
Interrupt handling classification uses small non zero values distinguishing IRQ handling from NMI handling.
Performance counter interrupt in guest test requires a valid VCPU with a guest handling marker and agreement between current NMI context and whether the marker denotes NMI handling.
Private memory presence reflects an arch flag on the VM, while readonly memory presence is the absence of protected state.
MSR read helper returns the 64 bit content of the requested register using the processor read instruction.
Host flags reserve low bits for guest mode, SMM mode and SMM inside NMI, and the maximum address space count is two.

Address space count collapses to one when private memory exists else two; VCPU slot selection follows SMM mode; shadow table role selection follows SMM role in one configuration and is fixed to zero in the other.
VCPU blocking and unblocking notifications delegate to vendor hooks, and IRQ bypass availability mirrors whether device posted interrupts are enabled.

Page track notification infrastructure pairs a sleepable read copy update structure with a notifier list head; each node supplies a write callback receiving guest address data length and node, plus a region removal callback receiving base frame page count and node.
An alternate configuration defines the notifier node as empty, indicating no tracking callbacks are available.
Guest paused check in this configuration never reports paused and performs no clearing.
Hypercall instruction selection uses runtime patching to choose between two virtualization call mnemonics based on processor feature for VMM call.

Numbered hypercall helpers with zero to four arguments first take a confidential guest path when that feature is active, otherwise issue the selected hypercall instruction with number and arguments in fixed registers and return the result register.
Secure guest hypercall with three arguments always issues the VMM call instruction directly with number and operands in fixed registers.
Default confidential hypercall helper reports device absence error.
Async page fault entry checks a static branch gate and on success delegates to the async handler with registers and token, otherwise reports not handled.
Paravirtual spinlock initialization is a no operation in this configuration.
Huge page split path can demand hundreds of descriptor objects for a single page, so callers must ensure the descriptor cache is prefilled to avoid allocation failure mid split.
Guest TLB invalidation by address may receive non canonical addresses from INVLPG emulation which implementations are permitted to ignore, and guest only flushes need not disturb GPA to HPA mappings.
Async page fault handling delegates to a routine owned by another dossier.
Static branch test used by async fault gate is owned by another dossier.
Alternate static branch test variant is owned by another dossier.
Zeroing allocator used for VM allocation is owned by another dossier.
